# Envoy Gateway compatibility table

<!-- Generated by `setura migrate convert --compat-report --format markdown`; do not edit. `make compat` regenerates it and TestEnvoyCompatDocInSync keeps it current. -->

Every Envoy Gateway policy field Setura knows about, the Setura setting it becomes and whether it is applied. The controller (`setura gateway run --kubernetes --envoy-compat`) and `setura migrate convert --from envoy-gateway` translate from this one table; how to switch is in [envoy-compat.md](envoy-compat.md).

133 fields: 46 Supported, 16 Partial, 71 Unsupported.

- **Supported**: translated and enforced.
- **Partial**: translated with the limits named in the notes.
- **Unsupported**: ignored; the policy status lists it with reason `Unsupported`, and a field that guards traffic (`basicAuth`, `oidc`, JWT and header authorization rules) makes the controller refuse the targeted traffic instead of serving it open.

## All policies

| Field | Status | Setura equivalent | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------------------|-------|
| `targetRefs` | Supported | targets resolved by the controller: Gateway, listener (sectionName), HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, rule (sectionName) | Envoy Gateway precedence: the most specific target wins |
| `targetRef` | Supported | same as targetRefs | deprecated single target |
| `targetSelectors` | Supported | labels select HTTPRoutes, GRPCRoutes or Gateways | matchLabels only; matchExpressions are not read |
| `mergeType` | Supported | StrategicMerge and JSONMerge merge the policy over the one it overrides | lists of objects with a name merge by name under StrategicMerge, other lists are replaced |
